clinician.final_diagnosis: Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (XGP) of the left kidney
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 3-year-old boy presented with a 1-year history of recurrent fever, dysuria, urinary frequency, and hematuria. Initial evaluation at a local dispensary showed urine dipstick findings suggestive of urinary tract infection, and he received multiple courses of antibiotics with temporary symptom relief followed by recurrence. No urine culture or imaging was performed at initial presentations. Subsequently, a repeat abdominal ultrasound revealed a large left renal mass (7.4×7.1×5 cm) with multiple cystic lesions, destroyed renal pelvis with calcific changes, and no extension to neighboring structures; the right kidney was normal. Based on clinical presentation and imaging findings, a diagnosis of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis was made. The patient underwent left radical nephroureterectomy with hilar lymph node resection. Intra-operatively, an enlarged yellowish-grey left kidney with multiple mesenteric and hilar lymph nodes was identified; the right kidney appeared normal on inspection. Histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis, showing macroscopically gross yellowish renal tissues and microscopically a renal histology infiltrated with foamy lipid-laden macrophages in a mixture of chronic inflammatory cells and fibrosis. Post-operatively, the patient recovered well and was discharged on post-operative day 10 after a 7-day course of intravenous Tazobactam/piperacillin.
